title: Korea Quantum Computing (KQC) to Go Public on Nasdaq via $80 Million SPAC Merger with Charlton Aria
source_used: Quantum Computing Report (full text read, citing a Business Wire release that was not read)
key_facts: KQC Quantum, Inc., parent of Korea Quantum Computing Co., Ltd., entered into a definitive business combination agreement with Charlton Aria Acquisition Corporation (Nasdaq: CHAR), a blank-cheque company.
The transaction values KQC at a pre-money equity valuation of $80 million ($11.00 per share), a pro forma valuation of about $215 million.
Closing is expected in the first half of 2027; the combined company would trade on Nasdaq as KQC.
KQC was founded in Busan in 2021; it is a hardware-agnostic quantum middleware and post-quantum security integrator, with the Qubiteer platform in beta since June 2026.
KQC also provides hardware security modules and is developing QuantumSpan, software for auditing cryptographic assets and managing post-quantum migration.
Net proceeds will fund conversion of enterprise pilots into full commercial deployments in finance, industry and transport in South Korea and Southeast Asia.
Conditions: a minimum cash closing condition of $30 million, shareholder approval and customary closing conditions.
quote_evidence: The transaction values KQC at a pre-money equity valuation of $80 million ($11.00 per share), implying a pro forma equity valuation of approximately $215 million.
The transaction includes a minimum cash closing condition of $30 million and is subject to shareholder approval and customary closing conditions.
why_it_matters_hint: A small quantum software firm agrees to a Nasdaq listing through a blank-cheque merger; the $80m is a valuation, not cash raised.
